title: Natural furniture polish
subtitle: A beeswax and lemon oil polish for oiled or waxed wood furniture
excerpt: A soft beeswax polish with lemon essential oil and olive oil for oiled and waxed wood furniture. Applied in a thin coat, buffed to a low sheen. Nourishes the wood and builds a protective wax layer over time. Not for lacquered or varnished furniture. Makes about 100 g of polish. Shelf life 18 months.
sourceNotes: Traditional furniture polish formulation: beeswax + carrier oil. A 1:2 ratio of beeswax to oil gives a soft, spreadable paste. Carnauba wax can be added at 10-15% to harden the finish, but is unnecessary for home furniture. Olive oil as carrier: food-safe, penetrates wood fibres, traditional for oiled furniture. Lemon essential oil: limonene provides mild cleansing and a characteristic furniture polish scent. Not for lacquered or polyurethane-varnished furniture: oil-based polishes cloud these finishes. Test on underside first.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles cleanly. 200 g is typically a year's supply for 4-6 pieces of furniture polished quarterly.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to use once set. Keeps 18 months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 18 months in a sealed tin. Beeswax is very stable. The olive oil can eventually oxidise, discard if the polish smells rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: A wax-based wood finish that fills the grain, repels water, and builds a protective layer with repeated application. Beeswax is softer than carnauba wax and gives a lower, more natural sheen.

with olive oil and lemon essential oil. It goes on oiled or waxed wood furniture, dining tables, chairs, sideboards. Applied in a thin layer, rubbed in with a cloth, left for 5 minutes, then buffed off. Not for lacquered or polyurethane-varnished furniture, which it can cloud. Makes about 100 g; lasts 18 months.

content.text: Put the beeswax and olive oil in a heatproof bowl over simmering water. Stir until the wax fully melts.
Remove from heat. Leave to cool to 40°C, then stir in the lemon essential oil.
Pour into the tin and leave undisturbed for 2 hours until set.

Test on the underside of the furniture first to check compatibility. Apply a small amount to a soft cloth and rub into the wood in circular motions. Leave for 5-10 minutes. Buff with a clean dry cloth to a soft sheen. Use quarterly, or more often on heavily used surfaces.
18 months in a sealed tin. Keep away from direct heat or sunlight. Discard if the polish smells rancid.
